name: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
notes: REDengine DX12 next-gen (same family as Cyberpunk 2077). LAUNCHED and played 11 Sep 2026, Apple M4, macOS 26.5.1, GPTK D3DMetal on the game-host tree; a person played in-world and quit from the game's own menu. Cannot reach §5 verified: REDengine writes no log of its own (same problem as ready-or-not), so there is no LoadMap line and no frame count to quote — `wyn profiles performance witcher-3` says so too. What was measured instead: `lsof` on the live bin\x64_dx12\witcher3.exe has external-3.0.bak/D3DMetal.framework, libd3dshared.dylib, libmetalirconverter.dylib and libdxccontainer.dylib open, with d3d12.dll and dxgi.dll taken as **builtins from the running tree** (the per-exe AppDefaults are d3d*=b) — while the DXMT natives another game left in system32 sat untouched, which is the AppDefaults mechanism working as intended. D3DMetal populated its own per-exe cache at d3dm/witcher3.exe/shaders.cache/MTLGPUFamilyApple9_0 (bytecode 6.3 MB, stage 12.3 MB, pipeline 131 KB, rootsignature 65 KB) during a first-run shader compile at ~105% CPU / 3.3 GB RSS. The launch env carries CX_GRAPHICS_BACKEND=d3dmetal — on winecx that, not WINEDLLOVERRIDES, is what selects the backend. Game wrote dx12user.settings: 1920x1080, FullScreenMode=1, VSync=true. Zero d3d/dxgi/metal errors in the wine log, zero new crash dumps. Prefer bin/x64_dx12/witcher3.exe over the DX11 x64 copy — `wyn play` picked it. Do not use Libraries.rgl or Libraries.vk. NOTE: the live D3DMetal is the directory named `Libraries/Wine/lib/external-3.0.bak` — `external` is a symlink to it. Not a mistake, but do not 'clean up' the .bak.
